questions.text: Which language is most of the reply in, and how does it address the customer? A reply in Spanish that adds one sentence in Portuguese to say which languages the chat serves is in Spanish.

options.es_usted: Spanish, addressing the customer as usted, or not addressing them at all
options.es_tu: Spanish, addressing the customer as tú or vos anywhere
options.pt_voce: Portuguese, addressing the customer as você, or not addressing them at all
options.pt_other: Portuguese, addressing the customer as tu, o senhor, or a senhora anywhere
options.mixed: Spanish and Portuguese, neither of them most of the reply

questions.text: Does the reply do what the turn's decision says for every request it lists (answer, ask the question it names, abstain, decline, ask for the confirm button, report the block, offer the handoff with its button, or report the handoff), say it will turn to the requests still queued, and say nothing that contradicts the decision?
The turn filed a handoff. Does the reply say that a person will follow up, give the case's reference, and promise no outcome and no time?
A confirmation to block a card ended unused in this turn. Does the reply say that the card was not blocked?

The bank's records conflict on a point the reply covers: a card listed as active past its expiration date, a code that says the card had expired on a transaction made before its recorded expiration, or a transaction dated before its card's opening. Does the reply state both facts without saying which one is right?
The reply explains a declined transaction by its response code. Does it give the code's meaning and nothing more, inferring no cause, advice, or pattern?
Does the reply, in its own words, avoid saying whether a charge is fraud and avoid promising, reporting, or opening a refund or a dispute?

The turn filed a handoff, and its free text is shown. Does the free text state what the customer asked for, match the verified facts without inventing any, and give the person who picks the case up enough to act on it?
How clear is the reply to the customer? 5: it reads easily and makes plain what happens next; 3: it can be understood with some effort; 1: it is confusing or contradicts itself.
